title: A service-quality remedy can return money while leaving individual access recovery unobserved
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission AT&T data-throttling enforcement and refund-administration record; eligible former unlimited-data customers are a remedy-program population, not a representative consumer sample
geography: United States federal consumer-protection enforcement involving former AT&T unlimited-data customers

observations.period: April 2024 initial refund distribution; August 2026 reissue route

denominator.unit: eligible former AT&T customers; current page does not publish a recipient denominator

initial_refund_distribution.unit: US dollars, more than, refunded in April 2024

reissue_method.value: Zelle payments to people who did not cash a check or accept a PayPal payment

service_harm.value: data speeds became so slow that common browsing and video streaming were difficult or impossible after a monthly threshold

individual_receipt_and_restored_access.value: not observed in the public refund page

observations.method: Official FTC refund-program page checked September 17, 2026; retain the completed April 2024 aggregate refund total separately from the August 2026 reissue route and do not treat either as a recipient-level recovery rate.
observations.uncertainty: The page does not publish the eligible or paid recipient denominator, individual amounts, failed-delivery count, service restoration, substitute connectivity, continued AT&T use, switching, trust, or later action. The initial refund total is rounded and reported as more than $5.6 million.
observations.subgroup: Eligible former AT&T customers whose unlimited-data service was allegedly throttled; earlier recipients, uncashed-check or unaccepted-PayPal recipients, reissued-payment recipients, and unknown-status customers are distinct groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A refund can compensate a past billing or service-quality injury without restoring the lost connectivity at the time it occurred; a reissue route can improve payment reach while leaving current provider choice and practical exit unchanged.

related_sources.claim: FTC lists AT&T Data Throttling Refunds as an active August 2026 refund program and identifies the reissue route administrator.

boundary: This record establishes a reported service-quality allegation, aggregate refund distribution, and current reissue route. It does not establish individual exposure, receipt, restored connectivity, service substitution, switching, trust, collective action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: FTC AT&T data-throttling refund HTML retrieved without retaining a repository copy
